subject.title: Control UI: Config upgrade/hardening suggestions should apply changes automatically with before/after diff and user acceptance, not direct users to edit files manually

question: Which Control UI security/auth recommendations may be applied automatically from browser recommendation cards, and what confirmation, diff, audit, restart, and allowlist policy must gate them?
rationale: The requested flow would persist auth and hardening config from browser-visible UI, so automation should not choose which security-sensitive settings are safe to mutate or downgrade automatically.

options.title: Allowlisted Recommendation Actions
options.body: Create a generic allowlisted action model that reuses config.patch/config.apply validation and shows exact diff, confirmation, dismissal, restart/audit, and redaction behavior for approved recommendations.

options.title: Keep Risky Auth Changes Manual
options.body: Leave auth/security downgrade and recovery suggestions as docs/manual guidance while allowing only low-risk non-auth recommendations to become one-click actions.

options.title: Split By Recommendation Class
options.body: Use separate policies for hardening, compatibility, and recovery recommendations so safe-by-default changes can be one-click while downgrade paths require stronger consent.

recommendation.title: Allowlisted Recommendation Actions
recommendation.body: Create a generic allowlisted action model that reuses config.patch/config.apply validation and shows exact diff, confirmation, dismissal, restart/audit, and redaction behavior for approved recommendations.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest combined recent history across Control UI Settings, secure Control UI auth, config validation, and product/security ownership evidence.
